quality_assessment: Chapter is comprehensive and accurate with excellent coverage of replacement functionality. Only minor clarifications needed regarding named group syntax compatibility.

issues.description: Chapter states PCRE2 mode supports '(?<name>pattern)' syntax but doesn't clarify that this syntax actually works in default Rust regex mode too
issues.current_content: You can also use named capture groups for more readable patterns. The syntax is `(?P<name>pattern)` in Rust regex (or `(?<name>pattern)` in PCRE2 mode).
issues.should_be: You can also use named capture groups for more readable patterns. The syntax is `(?P<name>pattern)` in Rust regex. The alternative syntax `(?<name>pattern)` is also supported in both Rust regex and PCRE2 mode.
issues.fix_suggestion: Clarify that (?<name>) works in both regex engines, not just PCRE2. The chapter shows one example using (?<name>) syntax (line 48) which could confuse readers about when each syntax applies. Based on tests and implementation, both syntaxes work interchangeably.
issues.source_reference: crates/pcre2/src/matcher.rs:78 (capture_names works for both), tests showing both syntaxes work

issues.description: Chapter mentions '--json' output includes replacement text but doesn't explain the exact JSON structure
issues.current_content: **With `--json`**: The JSON output includes a `submatches` array with replacement text in the `match` field
issues.should_add: Provide a brief example of JSON output structure with replacements, showing what the 'submatches' array looks like with replacement text
issues.source_reference: crates/printer/src/json.rs:106-112 (replacement method), JSON format documentation in same file

issues.description: The explanation that 'replacements only apply to matched lines, not context lines' could benefit from a concrete example
issues.current_content:
**With context flags** (`-A`, `-B`, `-C`): Replacements only apply to matched lines, not context lines

```bash
# Replace matches but keep context unchanged
rg 'error' -r 'ERROR' -C2
```
issues.should_be: Show a concrete before/after example demonstrating that context lines remain unchanged while matched lines are replaced
issues.fix_suggestion:
Expand the example to show actual output:
```bash
# Replace matches but keep context unchanged
rg 'error' -r 'ERROR' -C1
# If input is:
#   info message
#   error occurred
#   debug info
# Output shows:
#   info message          (context - unchanged)
#   ERROR occurred        (match - replaced)
#   debug info            (context - unchanged)
```
issues.source_reference: Behavior verified in crates/printer/src/standard.rs:741-780 replacement implementation

All syntax examples are accurate and tested
